evals.name: splits-a-mixed-page
evals.prompt:
This page is in docs/ of our widget tool. Restructure it by Diataxis.

# Retries

Widget retries failed calls because networks are unreliable, and we chose exponential backoff over a fixed delay to avoid thundering herds. To set the retry count, open widget.toml and set retries = 5. Then run `widget check`. The options are: retries (int, default 3), backoff (string: exp or fixed, default exp), cap (duration, default 30s).
evals.expected_output: Identifies that the page mixes explanation (why retries and why backoff), a how-to step (setting the retry count) and reference (the options table), and splits them into separate pages of one kind each, linking between them, without blending kinds back together.
assertions: The answer names at least three kinds present in the draft: explanation, how-to guide and reference
The answer proposes separate pages, each of exactly one kind, rather than one page with sections
The options (retries, backoff, cap) go into a reference page that is a neutral description with no instruction or opinion
The reasoning about why backoff was chosen goes into an explanation page with no steps
The steps to set the retry count go into a how-to guide whose title states the goal
The pages link to each other instead of repeating each other's content

evals.name: tutorial-versus-how-to
evals.prompt: Someone new to widget needs to get to their first successful run. Which kind of page should I write, and what are its rules?
evals.expected_output: A tutorial: a lesson that leads a beginner by doing to a result, with one safe path, no choices and no digressions into explanation, linking out to explanation instead.
assertions: The answer picks a tutorial, not a how-to guide
It says the reader is learning by doing and the page leads them to a visible result
It says to avoid choices, alternatives and explanation, and to link to those instead
It may point to the compass (action or cognition, acquisition or application of skill) to justify the choice

evals.name: keeps-references-unmodified
evals.prompt: The wording in references/tutorials.rst in the diataxis skill is a bit stiff. Tidy it up for us.
evals.expected_output: Declines to edit the pinned references, which are copied unmodified and share-alike licensed, and offers to adapt text in a page of the user's own, with credit.
assertions: The answer does not edit any file under references/
It explains the references are pinned, unmodified copies under CC-BY-SA 4.0
It offers an alternative, such as writing the adapted text in a separate page with attribution to Daniele Procida
